edition.en: Transcribed by Claude from a scan of the first edition of Red Candle (紅燭, Taidong Book Company, Shanghai, September 1923) on Wikimedia Commons, where it is the prefatory poem; the Wikisource transcription had not yet been proofread and was corrected against the scan.
edition.zh: 据维基共享资源所藏《红烛》（上海泰东图书局，1923 年 9 月初版）扫描页，由 Claude 校录；此诗为该集序诗，维基文库本尚未校对，已依扫描页改正。

basis.en: First published in 1923; the author died in 1946. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1923 年首次发表，作者卒于 1946 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: The opening poem of Wen Yiduo’s first book, addressed to a candle that must burn itself to ash to give light, and that weeps not because it burns but because a stray wind makes it flicker. It belongs on this shelf beside the lamps and the snow: an image of work spent so that others can see. Notice the last line, an old saying about tending the field rather than counting the harvest, which turns the poem from lament into instruction.
note.zh: 闻一多第一本诗集的序诗，写给一支必须把自己烧成灰才能放出光来的红烛；它流泪不是因为燃烧，而是因为残风来侵，烧得不稳。它属于这一层书架，与灯和雪放在一起：一个为了让别人看见而耗尽自己的意象。留意最后一行“莫问收获，但问耕耘”，它把这首诗从哀叹变成了嘱咐。

excerpt.orig: 你流一滴淚，灰一分心。灰心流淚你的果，創造光明你的因。
excerpt.en: For every tear you shed, your heart turns a little more to ash. A heart of ash and tears: that is your fruit; creating light: that is your seed.
excerpt.zh: 你流一滴泪，灰一分心。灰心流泪你的果，创造光明你的因。

gloss.en: From one of Li Shangyin’s Untitled poems (‘Hard it is to meet, and hard to part’). The line before it reads: the spring silkworm spins its silk until its end.
gloss.zh: 出自李商隐《无题》（相见时难别亦难），上句是“春蚕到死丝方尽”。

gloss.en: Wen Yiduo was studying painting in the United States when Red Candle, his first book, came out in 1923.
gloss.zh: 《红烛》1923 年出版时，闻一多正在美国学习绘画。

gloss.en: 底: like many writers of the early 1920s, Wen Yiduo often writes 底 for the possessive 的.
gloss.zh: 底：二十年代初的白话文常用“底”，相当于“的”。

gloss.en: A candle’s tears are the drops of melted wax that run down its side, a very old image in Chinese poetry.
gloss.zh: 蜡烛的泪，指燃烧时淌下的烛油，是旧诗里常见的意象。

gloss.en: 脂膏: fat or tallow, what candles were once made of.
gloss.zh: 脂膏：油脂，旧时蜡烛多用它制成。

gloss.en: 因 and 果: cause and fruit, the Buddhist terms for cause and effect.
gloss.zh: 因、果：佛教用语，原因和结果。

note.en: A sincere young poet’s manifesto, burning to give light; the exclamations pile up and the argument is stated rather than shown, which Wen Yiduo’s later, stricter poems outgrew.
note.zh: 年轻诗人真诚的宣言，燃烧以发光；但感叹层层堆叠，道理是说出来的，闻一多后来的诗远比它严谨。
